faq.whereIsMyVaultDataStored: Where is my vault data stored?
faq.theSelfHostedServerStoresAppRecordsI: The self-hosted server stores app records in SQLite and uploaded images as files in its data directory. The desktop app uses its own application-data folder on your computer. Your desktop and web vaults are separate unless the desktop app connects to that web server. Sharing a desktop vault with your phone uses that same vault, not a separate copy.
faq.eachVaultHasOneOwnerAccountCreatedOn: Each vault has one owner account, created on first use. A server asks for a one-time setup code from its log, so only the person running it can create the owner. The owner can require sign-in, and change the username or password, in Data & settings. If sign-in is turned off, only expose the server on a trusted network or behind an authenticated proxy. Desktop phone access always requires sign-in with the same Paintwarden account, even if local sign-in is disabled.
faq.canTheDesktopAppConnectToMyServer: Can the desktop app connect to my server?
faq.yesAtFirstLaunchChooseTheBundledLoca: Yes. At first launch, choose the bundled local server or connect to an existing Paintwarden server. You can switch that choice later in Data & settings.
faq.aDesktopVaultRunningOnYourComputerCa: A desktop vault running on your computer can be used without a separate remote server. A desktop app connected to a remote server needs that server to be reachable. The self-hosted web app needs its server running. For phone access to a desktop vault, the computer must stay awake with Paintwarden open.
faq.doesABackupIncludeMyPhotos: Does a backup include my photos?
faq.yesExportInDataSettingsSavesOneZipWi: Yes. Export in Data & settings saves one .zip with your records, miniature photos, and installed plugins. Restoring it lets you merge into the current vault or replace it. Your account and password are not included.
faq.whereDoThePaintsComeFrom: Where do the paints come from?
faq.fromPluginsPaintwardenDoesnTBundleAC: From plugins. Paintwarden doesn't bundle a catalog, so a new vault starts empty. Open Data & settings → Plugins and add a public GitHub repository or upload a plugin .zip to install its paints, color schemes, and miniature templates.
faq.canIShareMyOwnSchemesAndPaints: Can I share my own schemes and paints?
faq.yesCreatePluginInThePluginsDialogPac: Yes. Create plugin in the Plugins dialog packages your own paints, schemes, and templates as a .zip. Publish it as a public GitHub repository, or send the .zip so others can upload it.
faq.itComparesTheCatalogSScreenColorsAHi: It compares the catalog's screen colors. A high score does not guarantee two paints look identical on a model. Finish, opacity, primer, and lighting can change the result.
faq.doesTheRecipeConverterReplaceMyOrigi: Does the Recipe converter replace my original scheme?
faq.noItSavesANewReusableSchemeWithYourR: No. It saves a new reusable scheme with your reviewed paint choices. The original scheme remains available.
faq.canIAddPaintsThatNoPluginIncludes: Can I add paints that no plugin includes?
faq.yesUseAddPaintInThePaintsLibraryToCr: Yes. Use Add paint in the Paints library to create a custom color entry.

meta.phoneDescription: Share your desktop Paintwarden vault with your phone using Settings and a QR code, on Wi-Fi or Tailscale. Learn about access and privacy.
phone.title: At your desk. On your phone. Still yours.
phone.intro: Open your desktop vault in your phone’s browser. Enable access in Settings, choose an address and scan its QR code. No Paintwarden cloud account, subscription or separate mobile app is required.
phone.serverTitle: Enable access in desktop Settings, then scan the QR
phone.serverBody: In the desktop app, use “Use this computer” and finish account setup. Open Settings → Allow access from my other devices and turn it on; it is OFF by default. On the same trusted Wi-Fi, select a reachable address and scan its QR code with your phone’s camera, or open the address manually. Always sign in with the same Paintwarden account, even if desktop sign-in is disabled. Keep your Mac or computer awake with Paintwarden open. The phone uses the same vault, not a copy. Turn the setting off to stop network access.
phone.desktopNote: Optional always-on alternative: run Paintwarden with Docker Compose on your own server or NAS. Open that server’s address on your phone and sign in with its owner account. The desktop app can connect to that server too; remote mode does not keep an offline copy. This is separate from sharing the desktop’s local vault.
phone.remoteBody: For access away from home, install Tailscale on your computer and phone and join the same private network. With desktop phone access enabled, select the Tailscale address in Settings and scan its QR code. Keep the computer awake and Paintwarden open, then sign in with the same Paintwarden account. Tailscale offers a free Personal plan; limits and terms can change.
phone.remoteSafety: Do not forward this port from your router to the public Internet. Anyone who can reach your computer can reach the login page. Plain HTTP does not encrypt passwords or vault traffic; use only trusted Wi-Fi or Tailscale’s encrypted network. A direct Tailscale address is still an HTTP browser origin. For optional HTTPS, manually run the Tailscale Serve command shown in Settings on the same computer and follow the guide. Paintwarden does not run it for you. Tailscale is a separate, unaffiliated service with its own account and privacy policy.
phone.homeScreenTitle: A shortcut, not a second vault
phone.homeScreenBody: On iPhone or iPad, open your vault’s address in Safari, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen. On Android, use your browser’s Add to Home screen or Install option if offered. Menu names vary. The vault must remain reachable; this is not an offline app or a sync service.
phone.httpsNote: Use HTTPS with a trusted certificate for the best home-screen experience, especially on iOS. Plain HTTP on a LAN or private-network address may open as a browser shortcut and does not provide all secure-context features. Never bypass certificate warnings.
phone.privacyTitle: The Paintwarden app doesn’t collect your data.
phone.privacyBody: In local desktop mode, vault records and uploaded photos stay in your computer’s application-data folder. In server mode, they go to the server you choose. Its administrator controls storage, access, logs and backups. Owner accounts belong to that vault; there is no registration with us.
phone.networkBody: Packaged desktop apps check GitHub for updates. Plugin installation, checks and updates contact GitHub from your server; opening Plugins can update installed repository plugins in the background. URL image imports are fetched by the server, while displayed external images can contact their hosts from your browser. Links you open contact their destination.
phone.supportBody: The reviewed app code has no configured usage-analytics service or automatic diagnostic-upload endpoint. Save support bundle is optional: it saves a local file, not an upload. Desktop bundles include summary information and redacted log labels; browser exports contain summary JSON. Inspect files and screenshots before choosing to share them. Local logs and OS crash reports may still exist.
phone.privacyLink: Read the full privacy & network disclosure
phone.siteTitle: This website is separate from your vault
phone.siteBody: We keep aggregate visit counts for this website and delete raw access logs within 7 days. This does not describe logs on your own vault server or third-party services. The website remembers your chosen language in browser local storage.
home.phoneBody: In desktop Settings → Allow access from my other devices, turn on access (OFF by default). Choose an address and scan its QR code on the same Wi-Fi, or use Tailscale away from home. Keep your computer awake with Paintwarden open. Always sign in with the same Paintwarden account.
home.privacyTitle: The Paintwarden app doesn’t collect your data.
home.privacyBody: No usage analytics, no telemetry, no account with us. Your vault stays on your computer or your server. Updates, plugins and image links can contact third parties; support exports are optional local files.
